## TL;DR
The engineering report limit now applies only to the engineer-authored narrative. The prompt describes a soft target of around 1,000 words and a hard limit of 1,200 narrative words, the rejection error quotes the actual narrative count, and the tests prove that a large generated change summary cannot push an otherwise acceptable report over the cap.

## Work and rationale
The core behavior had already landed as a hotfix on main before this branch was cut: `MAX_WORDS` moved to 1,200, the second check against the finalized markdown was removed, and `wordCount` now stores the narrative count. Starting from a branch identical to main, I checked the remaining acceptance criteria instead of redoing the hotfix.

Two gaps mattered. First, the rejection message still described a generic report limit and called the measured value a "draft" count rather than the narrative count. I changed it to state the narrative word count and the narrative-only cap explicitly, so an engineer sees exactly what to shorten. Second, the prompt still framed 500–600 words as the target, while the task calls for a soft target around 1,000 and a hard cap at 1,200. I updated the prompt and both user-facing docs to describe that rule consistently, including that the generated change summary never counts.

The tests previously checked only that a many-file report was accepted. I strengthened them to assert that the stored `wordCount` equals the narrative count, that the generated markdown itself can exceed 1,200 words, and that the over-limit error contains both the measured narrative count and the 1,200-word cap. I also added a prompt-contract test so the guidance wording cannot silently drift back to the old cap.

## Approaches tried
I considered adding a word-count column to the Dev tab Report view to make the stored narrative count visible. The view currently renders the stored markdown (narrative plus the server-generated summary) and does not display a separate count at all, so there was no displayed number that could contradict the stored `wordCount`. Adding a column would have required a preview fixture and shot plan for a report history the preview board does not seed, which is disproportionate for this server-side bug. I left the view unchanged and covered the stored-count consistency with tests instead.

I also considered exporting the 1,200-word constant for reuse in tests. The existing test style keeps the cap as an expectation literal, which makes an accidental cap change fail loudly rather than move the expectation with the constant, so I kept the current structure.

## Challenges and blockers
The main challenge was that the task and the code disagreed at the start: the fix was already on main as a hotfix, but the task was still active and its branch matched main. I treated the hotfix as the baseline and scoped this round to the parts the task still required evidence for. No implementation blockers remain.

## Key learnings
A hotfix that lands on main does not close the task that motivated it; the remaining acceptance criteria still need tests and documentation to be verifiable. Generated bookkeeping should stay outside engineer-authored limits, and the error message is part of the contract: naming the narrative count and the same 1,200-word cap the prompt advertises prevents the loop described in the task. Prompt text, user docs, and tests should change together whenever a report rule changes.
